questions.stem: The Santosh Trophy, one of India's oldest sporting championships instituted in 1941, is associated with which sport?

options.option_text: Cricket — domestic first-class format
Football — national state-level championship
Field Hockey — zonal team competition
Kabaddi — inter-state Federation Cup level

questions.explanation: The Santosh Trophy is India's premier national football championship, contested among state and institutional teams. It is commonly confused with hockey trophies (like the Beighton Cup) because hockey historically dominated Indian sports headlines. Cricket's flagship domestic tournament is the Ranji Trophy, not the Santosh Trophy.

questions.stem: Which of the following tennis tournaments is NOT part of the four Grand Slam events in a calendar year?

options.option_text: Wimbledon Championship — held on grass courts in London
US Open — played on hard courts in New York, USA
Cincinnati Masters — an ATP Masters 1000 series event
French Open (Roland Garros) — clay courts in Paris, France

questions.explanation: The four Grand Slams are the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, and US Open. The Cincinnati Masters (Western & Southern Open) is an ATP Masters 1000 event — prestigious but a tier below the Grand Slams in prize money, points, and duration. Many candidates confuse Masters 1000 events with Grand Slams due to equal media coverage.

questions.stem: The Irani Cup in Indian cricket, held at the start of each domestic season, is contested between which two sides?

options.option_text: India A team and the current Indian Test squad members
Ranji Trophy defending champion vs Rest of India XI
The two Duleep Trophy finalists of the previous season
Defending Deodhar Trophy champion vs Vijay Hazare winners

questions.explanation: The Irani Cup is played between the Ranji Trophy defending champion and a Rest of India XI selected by BCCI selectors, traditionally inaugurating India's domestic season. The Duleep Trophy (zonal teams) and Deodhar Trophy (List A format) are separate competitions with different structures; conflating these is the most common error in exam answers.

questions.stem: The Nehru Trophy Boat Race, featuring iconic 'chundan vallam' (snake boats), is held annually on which water body in Kerala?

options.option_text: Ashtamudi Lake near Kollam in South Kerala
Periyar Lake at Thekkady, Idukki district
Punnamada Lake at Alappuzha (Alleppey), Kerala
Vembanad Lake at Kumarakom, Kottayam district

questions.explanation: The Nehru Trophy Boat Race is held on Punnamada Lake at Alappuzha (Alleppey). Vembanad Lake (near Kumarakom) is the most tempting distractor because Punnamada is a connected lagoon within the larger Vembanad backwater system — but the race venue is specifically Punnamada Lake, not Kumarakom. Periyar Lake is an inland reservoir entirely unrelated to boat races.

questions.stem: The Ashes urn, the symbolic prize of the England vs Australia cricket series since 1882, is traditionally said to physically contain what?

options.option_text: Ashes of a burnt cricket bail inside a small ceramic urn
A fragment of turf from the Lord's Cricket Ground, London
A miniature golden bat signed by W.G. Grace in 1882
A piece of the original leather ball used in that 1882 Test

questions.explanation: The Ashes urn is a small terracotta container believed to hold the ashes of a cricket bail (symbolising the 'death of English cricket' after Australia's first-ever Test win on English soil at The Oval in 1882). The Lord's turf and W.G. Grace bat options are fabrications designed to test whether candidates know the actual physical artefact versus the romantic legend surrounding it.

questions.stem: The 'Googly' — a wrist-spinner's delivery that turns opposite to a leg-break — is credited to which cricketer who first bowled it in first-class cricket around 1900?

options.option_text: B.J.T. Bosanquet, an English leg-spin bowler of the early 1900s
Clarrie Grimmett, the Australian wrist-spinner of the 1920s–30s
S.F. Barnes, the English medium-pace swing bowler of that era
Arthur Mailey, Australian leg-spinner who toured England in 1921

questions.explanation: B.J.T. (Bernard James Tindal) Bosanquet invented and popularised the googly around 1900, using it to devastating effect on England's 1903–04 Ashes tour. Clarrie Grimmett is the most tempting distractor because he is one of history's greatest leg-spinners, but he was born in 1891 and played in a later era; he refined wrist-spin variations but did not invent the googly. S.F. Barnes bowled a different style altogether.

questions.stem: The Sultan Azlan Shah Cup, a prestigious annual international hockey tournament held in Ipoh, is named after a ruler who also served as Malaysia's Head of State. He was the Sultan of which Malaysian state?

options.option_text: Selangor — the most populous state on Malaysia's west coast
Pahang — the largest state in Peninsular Malaysia by area
Perak — the state whose Sultan later became Yang di-Pertuan Agong
Johor — the southernmost state, bordering Singapore directly

questions.explanation: Sultan Azlan Shah was the Sultan of Perak who served as Malaysia's 9th Yang di-Pertuan Agong (constitutional monarch) from 1989 to 1994. The tournament is held in Ipoh, the capital of Perak. Selangor and Pahang are attractive distractors because both are politically prominent and large Malaysian states, but neither is associated with Sultan Azlan Shah or the Ipoh tournament venue.
